scopes.name: Social Organization of Animals
scopes.scope: Animal social organization is represented through finite, species-specific relational observations and interventions: cichlid aggression-defined hierarchy, vampire-bat sharing ties, bird foraging traditions, fish target choices and harvester-ant foraging regulation. These differ in membership, history, resources and observed times. Group structure and individual differences can both matter, while a common emergent substance, universal neural prerequisite, purely decentralized architecture and member-independent persistence are not established.
unresolved: Test complete versus partial carrier replacement, trait variation, environmental supply and relation persistence with matched observations before stronger member-independence claims.
A selective topology intervention and neural mediation would require their own preparation and group-level endpoints.

scopes.name: Collective Decision-Making
scopes.scope: Collective choice is operationalized by a declared group endpoint rather than a single universal aggregation rule. Golden-shiner experiments vary untrained membership against fixed, conflicting target-training groups and distinguish a preference-dependent effect from a reversed-target null. Published spatial/network models and social-choice concepts remain separate from fish observations. First arrival, majority alignment, consensus, truth, legitimacy and future group coordination are different quantities.
unresolved: Resolve the supporting-methods balanced-trial count conflict before numerical reconstruction.
Test group size independently of informational composition; compare accuracy, consensus failure and later behavior as separate endpoints.
Transfer to a new species or human institution needs new primary evidence and independent scientific review.

scopes.name: Mass Cognitive Distortion Regimes
scopes.scope: The proposed mass-distortion regime remains a hypothesis bounded by fact-check-defined diffusion, randomized rating bias, a numerical-estimation feedback experiment and partisan attitude responses. A factual error, preference, ideological extremity, approval score, retweet and confidence judgment are distinct. No persistent societal attractor, common cognitive pathology or universal network-amplification mechanism is established.
unresolved: Define factual calibration separately from policy preference and normative disagreement; preregister aggregation, persistence and contrary-outcome criteria before testing a mass regime.
Independent primary-data and mechanism checks remain necessary; the included studies are heterogeneous cases rather than independent replications of one phenomenon.

scopes.name: Collective Intelligence under Distributed Aggregation
scopes.scope: Collective intelligence denotes task-bound group-performance structure or accuracy under specified aggregation, not a single group mind. The two Woolley laboratory cohorts supply fitted cross-task patterns; Lorenz's feedback experiment supplies a contrary case where convergence and confidence do not deliver matching collective improvement. Group composition, interaction, aggregation and inference metrics remain separate.
unresolved: Reproduce task covariance and compare alternative factor/skill models; test prospective task and time transfer using independent groups and registered metrics.

scopes.name: Cooperation and Conflict in Large-Scale Societies
scopes.scope: Cooperation, sanctions, organized conflict and violence are distinct observables. Selected published public-goods/common-pool results constrain universal enforcement stories: communication can support bounded agreements, fines have costs and variable outcomes, institutional choices retain prior experience and antisocial punishment accompanies weaker contribution gains. Country background is observational. These games do not reconstruct wars, large alliances, political mobilization, intergenerational rivalry or a common society-wide regulatory dynamic.
unresolved: Read complete protocols/data, separate retaliation and enforcement, and study concrete dated collective-conflict cases before national-scale or historical claims.

scopes.name: Cultural and Linguistic Evolutionary Change
scopes.scope: Cultural change is represented through finite learner-to-learner language experiments and measure-specific migrant profiles, with historical cultural theory retained as bibliographic context. Transmission fidelity, structural alignment, task expressivity, cohort association and conditional transmission-model fit are different observables. These cases do not establish one historical evolutionary regime, a universal cultural replicator or an inevitable progression from institutions to language.
unresolved: Historical lineage reconstruction, competing transmission mechanisms and real communicative success require their own longitudinal observations and controls.
Read the corrected Kirby SI Table S7 and source response data before sequence-level numerical use.

scopes.name: Cultural Transmission, Recombination, and Idea Propagation
scopes.scope: Cultural propagation is represented through changing laboratory language outputs and fact-checked platform cascades. A chosen content variant, its observable transmission, a reconstructed cascade and the hypothesis of a self-replicating meme retain separate roles. Variation and retention can be studied without admitting a universal memetic unit, fixed cultural fitness or source-independent replication mechanism.
unresolved: Choose variant identity and transformation rules before counting copies, branching or extinction; directly test proposed learning and affective mediators.

scopes.name: Digital Social Networks
scopes.scope: Digital-network evidence separates randomized platform messages and score displays from observational rumor diffusion and conditional diffusion models. A site definition, one platform's experimental effect, a reconstructed retweet cascade and an inferred influence mechanism remain distinct. No universal recommendation algorithm, self-stabilizing digital regime or necessary cognitive hierarchy is established.
unresolved: Disentangle platform selection, algorithmic treatment and interpersonal exposure before transferring intervention findings to another platform or time.

scopes.name: Dynamics of Economic Markets
scopes.scope: Market dynamics are reconstructed as transactions under explicitly supplied trading rules, values and information. Smith's classroom auctions provide conditional price/volume behavior; Hayek supplies a separate conceptual dispersed-knowledge argument. Neither is a complete model of production, financial crisis, trust, macroeconomic stability or a universal decentralized social regime.
unresolved: Read complete experimental charts, the separate correction item and alternative rule treatments; reconstruct monetary incentives and out-of-laboratory transfer before quantitative market claims.

scopes.name: Structures of Human Society
scopes.scope: Human societal structures are a representation of specified relations, institutions and spatial aggregations, not one experimentally isolated ordering substance. Historical constitutive rules and observational urban indicators offer different evidence. Persistence across office holders, generations, territories and social strata needs its own longitudinal sampling; none is proved merely by calling society a pattern.
unresolved: Specify institution/population boundaries and collect turnover-spanning historical evidence before strengthening persistence, kinship or cumulative-complexity claims.

scopes.name: Formation of Influence Networks
scopes.scope: Influence is represented through specific randomized exposure effects and a separately declared diffusion-model report. A following/friendship link, visible popularity, an estimated treatment effect and a persistent directed influence coefficient are not interchangeable. Network stabilization, generalized brokerage advantage and a universal influential elite remain unestablished.
unresolved: Estimate influence with exposure assignment and alternatives to homophily/common causes; independently test stability across topics, platforms and time.

scopes.name: Superorganism Behavior in Insect Colonies
scopes.scope: The colony category organizes experimentally perturbed harvester-ant foraging, local cue composition, observed departure timing and duration-dependent recovery. It does not combine all insect taxa, castes, task types and times into one measured colony organism. Foraging traffic, contacts and vestibule occupancy retain their own endpoints and nulls; chemical dose, necessary encounter threshold, complete feedback closure, construction, reproduction and colony-level irreducibility remain unestablished by these preparations.
unresolved: Resolve Greene's nanogram/microgram conflict before quantitative cue-dose or carrier interpretation.
Observe nondeparting as well as departing ants and selectively perturb candidate mediation before admitting encounter necessity or a complete feedback mechanism.
Generalization to brood care, construction, reproduction, other species, complete turnover or whole-colony resource homeostasis needs additional primary preparations.

scopes.name: Evolution of Complex Social Institutions
scopes.scope: Institutional change is a source-bounded historical question about specified rules, offices, practices and their alteration. A constitutive document defines continuity and powers; short laboratory treatments reveal different outcomes under nominally similar institutions, sanction costs and prior-experience-dependent selection. These supply neither intergenerational reproduction, universal path dependence, an autonomous institutional force nor one constructor for law, religion, education, science and finance.
unresolved: Reconstruct a specified institution's records across dated reforms, failures and membership turnover before quantitative path-dependence or reproduction claims.

scopes.name: Epistemic Markets and Knowledge Valuation
scopes.scope: Knowledge valuation is a declared scope for attention, assessment and credibility processes, illustrated here by randomized public-rating effects and externally fact-checked diffusion. Approval, visibility, reputation, truth and evidential warrant remain distinct. Historical sociology/philosophy is bibliographic context; a common decentralized market mechanism across science, media, education and policy is not measured.
unresolved: Define an independent accuracy or evidential-warrant criterion before evaluating epistemic success; test scientific and institutional valuation with their own primary preparations.

scopes.name: Political and Governance Structures
scopes.scope: Governance structures are represented as named constitutive offices, decision procedures and specified powers, separately from measured cooperation or realized authority. The original Charter supplies a documentary institutional example; common-pool experiments distinguish communication, monitoring, sanction costs, combined institutional trajectories and historically selected sanction choices. Definitions of jurisdiction or legitimacy do not themselves establish effective compliance or a universal route from informal norms to states.
unresolved: Read complete governance experiments and longitudinal institutional records, separating rule specification, actual enforcement, legitimacy measures and outcomes.

scopes.name: Recurrent Social Practices
scopes.scope: Repeated social practice is a descriptive category for temporally recurring coordinated actions, with experimentally seeded bird foraging techniques and recurring bat-sharing ties as bounded animal examples. Technique transmission and nine-month retention do not establish every human practice, explicit expectations, automatic conflict reduction or universal dependence on hierarchy. Original practice-theory books remain attributed as unread conceptual sources.
unresolved: Human practice-theory arguments require their own read passages and source-appropriate historical or observational evidence.
Test coordination cost, expectation, hierarchy necessity and full participant replacement separately from observed technique fidelity.

scopes.name: Sociogenesis of Shared Information Environments
scopes.scope: Shared information environments are represented as source-specific distributions of media salience, visible platform cues and fact-checked rumor exposure. The Chapel Hill media/public correlation, randomized platform response and observational diffusion are different preparations. A societal attractor, common credibility field, centralized-control independence or fixed sociogenetic construction order remains a hypothesis rather than a measured system state.
unresolved: Specify units, exposure distributions, salience measures, accuracy criteria and observation horizons before testing a persistent societal state or attractor.

scopes.name: Social Identity and Group Belonging
scopes.scope: Social identity is represented through a bounded minimal-categorization allocation report, differentiated migrant affiliation/orientation profiles and an acute exclusion imaging task. Behavioral allocation, questionnaire affiliation, cultural-group classification and distress/BOLD are different measurements. These sources do not establish one persistent social-system identity property, necessary national symbolism or unavoidable out-group conflict.
unresolved: Separate self-identification, externally assigned group, allocation preference and hostility in matched tests; obtain the full primary categorization protocol before detailed causal or numerical use.

scopes.name: Societal Feedback on Individual Neurodynamics
scopes.scope: The proposed societal-to-neural link is bounded here by acute ordered social-exclusion imaging and an already admitted rat maternal-environment observation and mediation hypothesis. Social context, reported distress, BOLD, chromatin profiles and long-term neural plasticity retain different populations, times and evidence types. No direct universal downward/diagonal causal law, chronic institutional control variable or minimum neural carrier is established.
unresolved: Define chronic social exposure and a repeated neural endpoint; separate fixed-order effects, distress reporting and selective neural mediation.
Read the original imaging supporting Methods and reproduce analysis before quantitative neural use; rat maternal-care mechanisms retain their existing reporting and species limits.

scopes.name: Social Norms and Conventions
scopes.scope: A convention is represented through the particular coordination and incentive setting in which it is observed; a moral or prescriptive norm is not identical to naming agreement. The naming experiment supplies finite adoption successes/failures after a committed minority is introduced, while punishment records show that sanctions need not improve cooperation. Shared expectations, reputation, exclusion and moral obligation need separate measurements.
unresolved: Measure normative/empirical expectations separately and test alternative incentives, network structures and populations before transferring naming-game results.

scopes.name: Social Exchange and Resource Coordination
scopes.scope: Physical resource transfer, task-specific food acquisition and normative human exchange are represented separately. Captive bat studies provide observed food-sharing relationships and competing explanations; ant studies provide supplied-cue and return-flow interventions, not measurements of a complete social metabolism. Redistribution, obligations, institutions, queueing and scalability remain conceptual or unresolved unless their own source-bound observations support them.
unresolved: Historical reciprocity and redistribution claims require reading the original arguments and comparing appropriate human evidence.
Measure survival, resource balance, conflict, queue discipline and allocation under selective perturbations before stronger stabilization or collective-metabolism claims.

scopes.name: Social Roles and Stratification
scopes.scope: Aggression-defined dominance, influence, learned competence, worker task and voluntarily conferred human prestige are distinguished rather than treated as interchangeable rank. Cichlid experiments support context-sensitive hierarchy formation and changing individual positions. They do not establish human authority, obligation, responsibility, durable positions surviving complete occupant replacement or one hierarchy required by all social coordination.
unresolved: Distinguish rank, task, access, prestige and normative roles in new source-matched experiments.
Resolve the original table/prose hierarchy percentage conflict before numerical replay; retain protocol differences when testing mechanisms.

scopes.name: Transculturation and Hybridization of Traditions
scopes.scope: Transculturation is a declared historical-cultural research scope, illustrated by heterogeneous migrant-group profiles and bounded laboratory reorganization of transmitted labels. A mixed or intermediate measurement does not alone prove reciprocal historical transformation, creation of a novel tradition or irreducibility to cultural sources. Colonial power, unequal contact and adaptation claims require separately identified historical evidence.
unresolved: Read and compare the relevant historical primary materials; define a cultural variant, contact direction, coercion context and persistence horizon before claiming reciprocal hybrid tradition formation.
Respect the 2018 migrant-table correction and measure-specific nulls; no group-essentialist or uniform assimilation inference follows.

scopes.name: Global Governance and Supranational Institutions
scopes.scope: Transnational governance is reconstructed through specific historical constitutive organs, procedures and powers, rather than an undifferentiated global object. The 1945 Charter distinguishes organizational design, sovereign-member principles and asymmetric decision/enforcement provisions. These definitions differ from current amended rules, observed compliance, legitimacy, democratic authority and causal effectiveness; the original interdependence/regime works retain their actual reading boundaries.
unresolved: For a specified institution, review dated amendments, decision records, implementation and independently measured outcomes before strengthening efficacy, persistence or legitimacy claims.

scopes.name: Morphogenesis of Cities and Urban Dynamics
scopes.scope: Cities are operational spatial/population aggregations whose observed indicators and scaling depend on the national system, boundary, cutoff and proxy. Source-reported urban regularities are retained together with boundary-sensitive contrary evidence. Morphological formation, transport, segregation, infrastructure inertia and causal urban feedback need distinct data; no autonomous urban attractor, biological identity or universal growth law is inferred from aggregate correlations.
unresolved: Read complete original data/fitting methods and test boundary robustness, longitudinal formation and causal interventions independently of population correlations.
